It was a one-time thing, but still, it's cheating. That happened a month ago. Now, today, I found out who the girl is through a mutual coworker. I messaged her trying to look out for another girl, but it backfired. I sent screenshots and told her what happened, saying she deserved better. She responded by saying they had already discussed it and that I should never contact her again. Her response was really rude. I'm wondering if I should have said anything. I thought I was doing the right thing because I wouldn't want to be in her shoes if my boyfriend was cheating. But now I feel dumb for bringing it up since she said they were over it. So, is it right or wrong for me to have told her? Let me break it down. On one hand, I felt like I was being honest and trying to help her. If I were in her position, I'd want to know if my partner was cheating. It's about transparency and fairness. Maybe I thought by telling her, I was giving her the chance to make an informed decision about her relationship. On the other hand, I might have overstepped. The guy had already told me, and maybe it was his responsibility to tell her, not mine. By contacting her, I might have interfered in their relationship, which could have caused unnecessary hurt or tension. Plus, she was rude, which probably made me feel bad, and maybe I should have just let it go. I also need to consider the impact of my actions. She was already aware, as she said they had discussed it. So, by contacting her, I might have just reminded her of the situation, which could have been painful for her. Maybe she wanted to move on and didn't need the reminder. Another point is the way I approached her. Sending screenshots and messages might have come off as accusatory or confrontational. Maybe a more gentle approach would have been better, but even then, it's her choice whether to accept the information or not. I also have to think about my own feelings. I felt guilty enough to tell her, but then I felt dumb for bringing it up. It's possible that I was trying to absolve myself of guilt by telling her, but it ended up causing more problems. In terms of right or wrong, I think it's a bit of both. On one side, honesty is important, but on the other, respecting boundaries and not interfering in others' relationships is also crucial. Maybe the right thing would have been to let the guy handle it since he was the one who cheated. Or perhaps, if I felt compelled to tell her, I should have done it in a more considerate way, without sending evidence or being confrontational. I also wonder about the consequences. By telling her, I might have affected her trust in her partner or in others. It's a heavy thing to carry, and maybe it's better left between the two people involved. In the end, I think I overreacted. The guy had already told me, and it was his responsibility to tell her. By contacting her, I might have made things worse for both of us. It's possible that I should have kept my mouth shut and let them handle it themselves.
